newsitem.title: USA: Apple slashed costs in fiscal Q4-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Apple slashed costs in fiscal Q4-analysts.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc managed to turn a profit in its final quarter of fiscal 1996 by sharply cutting costs more than Wall Street had expected, analysts said.

"It is a shock. Its seems they've brought the break-even point for their business down pretty dramatically," said Daniel Kunstler, computer industry analyst at JP Morgan, after the company surprised investors with a fourth quarter profit.
"This is very encouraging," he added. Apple said operating expenses before a restructuring adjustment had been reduced to $505 million from $519 million in the June third quarter.

Apple stunned Wall Street by posting profits for its fourth fiscal quarter of $0.20 a share, including a gain of $17 million or $0.14 a share related to an adjustment for prior period restructuring charges.
Wall Street analysts had expected Apple to post a loss of around $0.30 a share, according to First Call.
